what: Use plausible values in secondary analyses
title: FARL: An Applied Guide for Unidimensional Assessments
text: Run intended analysis separately every plausible-value column combine resulting estimates uncertainty. average plausible values first analyze single average observed score. following helpers summarize overall spread across set plausible values. variance.sample() averages respondent-level variance across PV datasets, variance.cal() also accounts variation among PV dataset means. substantive regression, repeat model plausible value store coefficient sampling variance. stored estimates can combined using multiple-imputation pooling procedure appropriate target analysis.
code: variance.sample <- function(theta_matrix) {   theta_matrix <- as.matrix(theta_matrix)   mean(apply(theta_matrix, 2L, stats::var)) }  variance.cal <- function(theta_matrix) {   theta_matrix <- as.matrix(theta_matrix)   number_of_pvs <- ncol(theta_matrix)   within_variance <- variance.sample(theta_matrix)   between_variance <- stats::var(colMeans(theta_matrix))    within_variance +     (1 + 1 / number_of_pvs) * between_variance }  pv_matrix <- farl_pvs$data  variance.sample(pv_matrix) variance.cal(pv_matrix) analysis_data <- data.frame(   outcome = sim_a1$X[, 1],   group = sim_a1$X[, 2] )  pv_results <- lapply(   seq_len(ncol(farl_pvs$data)),   function(pv_index) {     model_data <- transform(       analysis_data,       plausible_value = farl_pvs$data[, pv_index]     )      model <- lm(plausible_value ~ group, data = model_data)      data.frame(       pv = pv_index,       estimate = coef(model)["group"],       sampling_variance = vcov(model)["group", "group"],       row.names = NULL     )   } )  pv_results <- do.call(rbind, pv_results) pv_results

what: FARL: Use Factor-Augmented Regularized Latent Regression for Large-Scale Assessment
title: FARL: Use Factor-Augmented Regularized Latent Regression for Large-Scale Assessment
text: FARL implements factor-augmented regularized latent regression (FARLR) large-scale assessments. FARLR addresses high-dimensional, strongly dependent background variables decomposing variation common latent factors idiosyncratic components. components enter latent regression, sparse regularization selects parsimonious set relevant covariates. structure stabilizes estimation, preserves interpretability selected background variables, supports plausible-value generation group-level inference. multidimensional assessments, FARL jointly estimates regression coefficient matrix full latent residual covariance Gaussian variational expectation-maximization. Farlr_mml(): Provides unified interface fitting FARLR models. Use method = "FARLR_EMM" importance-sampling-based expectation-maximization-maximization estimation, method = "FARLR_Debias" correct shrinkage bias regularized coefficients. Farlr_drawPVs(): Draws plausible values posterior latent-trait distributions implied fitted FARLR model. Dire_mml(): Fits PCA-based DIRE latent regression used comparison approach high-dimensional background variables. Dire_drawPVs(): Draws plausible values fitted DIRE models. MFARLR_mml(): Fits multidimensional FARLR combining dimension-specific sparse screening joint GVEM estimation. MFARLR_drawPVs(): Draws correlated multidimensional plausible values fitted MFARLR model. MDIRE_mml() MDIRE_drawPVs(): Fit multidimensional PCA-based comparison model generate plausible values.

what: FARLR Marginal Maximum Likelihood Estimation — Farlr_mml
title: FARLR Marginal Maximum Likelihood Estimation — Farlr_mml
text: Fits Factor-Adjusted Regularized Latent Regression (FARLR) model using marginal maximum likelihood (MML) framework. function serves unified interface supports multiple estimation strategies, including "FARLR_EMM" "FARLR_Debias". Latent traits integrated using Monte Carlo approximation, regression parameters estimated regularization. Depending specified method, algorithm either employs EM–M–type iterative scheme post-selection debiasing procedure.

title: FARLR Marginal Maximum Likelihood Estimation — Farlr_mml
text: X Matrix. Covariate design matrix latent regression model, typically dimension n x p. Y Matrix. Observed item response matrix dimension n x J. parTab Data frame. Item parameter table containing least columns slope, difficulty, guessin, used define item response model. n_sam Integer. Number Monte Carlo samples per individual used approximate integrals latent traits. Defaults 5. method Character string. Estimation method used. Supported values include: "FARLR_EMM" Iterative FARLR estimation based EM–M–type   updating scheme regularization. "FARLR_Debias" FARLR estimation regularized variable   selection followed post-selection debiased refit. Defaults "FARLR_EMM". lambda Numeric vector. Candidate regularization parameters used penalized regression. Defaults seq(0.1, 0.5, = 0.1). delta.criteria Numeric. Convergence tolerance iterative updates. Defaults 1e-3. iter.max Integer. Maximum number iterations allowed value lambda. Defaults 200. window.size Integer. Window size sliding-window averaging coefficient updates used stabilize iterative estimation. Defaults 50. verbose Logical. TRUE, progress messages iteration status displayed model fitting. Defaults TRUE.

title: Simulated Dataset: 1D FARLR-Style Mixed-Format Item Responses — sim_a2
text: latent trait generated linear predictor additive noise: \(\theta = F \beta + E \nu + e\), \(e\) scaled   match target SNR. default dataset contains 15 items: eight 3PL items seven three-category GPCM items. Item slopes generated \(a_j \sim \mathrm{Lognormal}(0, 0.25)\). 3PL item, probability correct response $$P(Y_{ij}=1 \mid \theta_i) = c_j + (1-c_j)       \mathrm{logit}^{-1}\{a_j(\theta_i-b_j)\},$$ mirt intercept computed \(d_j=-a_jb_j\). GPCM item three response categories, 0, 1, 2, two step difficulties, \(b_{1j}\) \(b_{2j}\). converted mirt intercept parameterization $$d_{0j}=0,\quad d_{1j}=-a_jb_{1j},\quad       d_{2j}=-a_j(b_{1j}+b_{2j}).$$ Responses simulated using item-specific values itemtype, 3PL lower-asymptote parameters supplied guess argument mirt::simdata().
